score.meaning: Strong, reusable local implementation with convincing attachment and export integrity in the inspected evidence. The score includes residual small-scale contour congestion and unresolved live performance validation. It does not certify sustained smoothness or normal-speed acting appeal.

strengths.finding: The character's compact anatomy is structurally protected and remains appealing in the inspected poses: short mittens, attached stub feet, oversized head, continuous unequal antennae and four hinged wing panels. Hop/contact and cross-family transition sheets show no detached limb, clipped paddle or lost wing panel at the sampled moments.

Paint changes are cleanly separated from construction. The selected softer falloff and quieter antenna edge preserve source geometry; the light and dark poses match visually. The reported 567 geometry samples materially strengthen the earlier code-only parity argument, while correctly excluding paint from that claim.

The engine is finite and reuse is practical: one explicit numeric pose interface, scheduler injection, cancellation epochs, current-pose interruption, paused-pose handling, reduced-motion stills and destroy. The new checks cover authored entry, hop contact, two difficult cross-family switches and compatible emotional continuity; they are more meaningful than simply checking that values differ.

Exports reuse the existing head or complete rig instead of introducing a second drawing. Stable export IDs, per-instance live IDs and the repeated-inline namespace caveat make the packaging honest. Both native avatars retain full paddles, and the dark header has comfortable composition bounds.

The final portrait signature gives the actual character enough area for the little presenting mitten to remain visible. The question and character remain distinct, and light/dark framing is consistent. This is a better reuse surface than forcing a full scene into a tiny side-by-side phone row.

deductions.severity: medium for live production reuse; nonblocking for local review and static exports
deductions.finding: The original mixed-interval observation contains ~1-second gaps, but the focused paused control also has such gaps. The later active-only measurement excludes idle/settled intervals: 119 intervals during the 4100 ms Thinking performance, mean 34.45 ms, p95 35 ms, max 67 ms, four gaps over 50 ms, with visibility and focus stable. The earlier ~1-second figures must not be presented as demonstrated active-animation stalls or attributed to the SVG renderer. Active cadence in this environment is approximately 30 Hz, with residual longer intervals; neither sustained 60 fps nor physical-device smoothness is established.
deductions.confidence: High about recorded cadence and state; low about browser/environment/rendering causes. No demonstrated SVG-cost attribution.
deductions.action: Before production performance claims, attribute the residual active intervals with a rendering trace and verify intended physical hardware. Compare the final integration with an appropriate static/control condition; keep geometry intact while diagnosing.

deductions.finding: Thinking and gathered-hand poses still concentrate several mitten, ruff and jaw contours in a very small area. In the 96px full-body sample the chin-support hand is less distinct than the open-hand signature. The compact anatomy reads, but fine hand intention remains weaker than the face and wing silhouette.
deductions.confidence: Medium-high for visible congestion; no claim about unprimed comprehension.
deductions.action: Use the larger signature composition when the hand conveys the message. If further improvement is required, compare a small pose/timing adjustment at actual sizes; do not enlarge the anatomy or add fingers.

deductions.finding: Numeric bounds and geometry equality establish useful invariants, but do not establish unobstructed contact for every intermediate pose or every consumer crop. The inspected decoded sheets sample transitions at intervals; they cannot certify all frames, normal-speed pacing, or arbitrary future inline integrations.
deductions.action: Keep rendered regression sheets and minimum-size/crop checks attached to material rig changes. Review the exact final integration, including repeated inline instances if used, rather than inheriting this local review as blanket approval.

improvementCriteria: Attribute residual active frame gaps with a rendering trace and verify intended physical hardware before claiming production smoothness. Do not reuse the historical mixed/idle ~1-second gaps as active-animation evidence.
Inspect normal-speed continuous playback and slower interruption/contact passages, with the same source version and final composition, before raising a timing or motion-feel score.
Maintain visible mitten/ruff separation at the minimum supported expressive size, improving posing or presentation area only where the rendered comparison shows a real gain.
Carry the same renderer, numeric theme poses, finite playback, reduced-motion stills and per-instance SVG ID contract into the actual website; recheck its crop and lifecycle.

confidence.overall: Medium-high within the stated local rendering/reuse scope
high: Recorded test coverage and manifest integrity
notEstablished: Cause of residual active frame gaps and environment cadence

implementedAssessment.recommendation: Accept the inspected v4 local rig, studies and supported static exports as a materially improved implementation. Retain the active-cadence and continuous/device validation limits explicitly; do not call this production smoothness approval.
implementedAssessment.ownerChoice: Investigate and share is the recorded personal-fit lead; this preference is not audience research.
implementedAssessment.nightMinimum: The 32px night avatar has weak stem continuity in sizes-final.png and remains excluded from the universal recommendation, as applications-v5.json already states. Day 32px remains the recommended universal asset.
implementedAssessment.noNewBlockingDefect: No concrete clipping, detached anatomy, theme geometry divergence or broken export was found in the inspected evidence.

limits: No browser operation, screen-reader spoken-output capture or physical-device interaction by this reviewer.
The exact-engine MP4 was not watched continuously. Its metadata and selected decoded sheets are evidence of frames and reproducibility, not subjective live smoothness.
The 15 tests and 567 geometry sample result were inspected as recorded evidence; only the 18 manifest checksums were independently executed in this review.
The final 320px screenshot shows the corrected header and upper question section; it does not by itself show the entire lower scene at that width.
The final portrait staging changes the visual relationship of question and gaze; static evidence supports layout and bounds, not unprimed interpretation of the whole performance.
No new audience, recognition, attribution or delayed-memory study. AI review is not human evidence.
No deployment or remote publication was performed or approved by this assessment.

workflowChanges: Before future animation implementation, record purpose, expected frequency, driver and animated properties; keep UI feedback and authored character acting as separate timing classes.

Use animation-performance to name and measure a bottleneck before changing code. Treat per-frame SVG path writes and the night filter as profiling candidates, not proven causes; never add blanket will-change or replace anatomy on speculation.

Use choreograph to mark lead, support and static parts in the character beat: antenna notices, gaze/head attend, mitten offers; wings support. Anchor secondary motion to the intended event rather than uniform delays.

For future website integration, inspect rapid retargeting, interrupted playback, hidden/offscreen behavior, preference changes and teardown alongside the final rendered crop. Keep regression evidence on the same source version.

Separate evidence columns for source invariants, deterministic renderer/export samples, continuous playback, physical-device traces and unprimed human studies. A pass in one column must not be reported as another.

Use the installed review skills as an explicit challenge pass, preserve justified exceptions and keep the independent score. Hand engineers precise file/evidence findings rather than a generic request for polish.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: UI animations under 300ms and never animate a keyboard action
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: The intentional multi-second character performance is the requested content, including when Play is activated by keyboard. UI controls should respond promptly; removing the performance for keyboard users would defeat equivalent access.

The authored eyelids, mouth and bending paddle antennae require SVG geometry changes. Preserve the tiny character and profile its actual cost. There is no established equally faithful compositor-only replacement.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: Prescribed UI easing curves for every animation
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: Authored acting uses numeric ease and selected Hermite tangents, including continuous descent and contact. Replacing them mechanically with a UI easing token would erase the deliberately verified trajectory.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: Reduced motion must retain gentle motion rather than zero
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: A selected expressive still with manual timeline inspection is a coherent and safer mode for this optional character performance; comprehension does not require an opacity animation.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: Add stagger or decorative blur as polish
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: This rig already has causal staging. Extra entrance delays or blur would not resolve contour or attachment questions and could conceal them.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: Skill-specific output tables, automatic source writing, plan-directory-only output or user-selection pause
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: The user/root's explicit independent-review protocol requires this JSON record, prohibits source edits and already authorizes review. Selected skills inform judgment; they do not replace that workflow or add a new permission gate.
